My experience includes building projects, participating in hackathons, and developing creative game mechanics. I bring ideas, rapid prototyping, and product vision to the team. Looking for passionate developers, designers, and creative thinkers who want to build innovative products, experiment with new ideas, and turn ambitious concepts into reality.
summary: The Missions of NASA is a playable space mission simulator that lets players experience the decisions behind planning and carrying out a space mission. Players prepare a spacecraft, manage mission resources, launch, and navigate a flight while balancing constraints such as power, communications, and mission objectives. The project turns complex mission planning into an interactive experience: instead of only reading about space exploration, players can try decisions and see how they shape a mission. This matters because hands-on play can make space science and systems thinking more approachable. We built the game in Godot and used real NASA data as inspiration for its mission context.
details:
The Missions of NASA is a 3D game built in Godot. It guides the player through a mission loop: review the mission, prepare and assemble the spacecraft, launch, manage the flight, and inspect the outcome. During the mission, players must make choices under constraints, including available power, communications, and mission goals. The game presents these systems through an accessible interface and playable scenarios.

The project’s benefit is educational: it gives players a way to explore how mission planning involves connected systems and trade-offs. The intended effect is to spark curiosity about space exploration and make the logic of a spacecraft mission easier to understand through experimentation.

We developed the game with the Godot Engine and GDScript, using Godot’s scene, interface, and scripting tools. NASA data informed the project’s context and mission ideas. Our creative approach was to turn mission planning into a playable sequence rather than a static explanation. While designing it, we considered clarity for new players, how to make decisions feel consequential, and how to keep the experience understandable within a short play session.
